transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky tells NPR the Trump administration has warned it
could cut off intelligence sharing with Ukraine unless the Ukrainians stopped long-range drone
strikes on Russian oil refineries.
NPR's Rana Gekisic spoke to Zelensky in Kyiv.
Zelensky told NPR that the Trump administration's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel
will not bring down fuel prices.
He says the Iran war has blocked fuel transport through the Strait of Hormuz.
"Mostly people in the world know why their prices on any kind of energy, including diesel,
raised up, why they increased.
Because of blocking the Strait of Hormuz.
Everybody understands it."
President Trump blames Ukraine for rising diesel prices.
He has demanded Ukraine stop its deep strikes on Russian energy sites.
Zelensky says Ukraine wants to weaken the Kremlin's ability to wage war.
He says Ukraine will not stop these strikes unless Russia also stops attacking Ukraine's
energy grid.
Joanna Gekisic, NPR News, Kyiv.
On his way out of the White House today, President Trump took questions about where the US stands
with Ukraine on intel.
We are helping them and we are sharing intel, we want the war to end.
So we're working with them and with Russia on getting the war to end.
President Trump en route now to Alaska.
He is traveling more than 3,000 miles to a Republican stronghold in an attempt to bolster
Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
The long trip underscores GOP concerns about losing control of Congress in the midterm
elections in three weeks.
Trump is scheduled to lead a rally in Wasilla, the town north of Anchorage that became politically
famous as the hometown of former Republican vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin.
It is also the headquarters of the famous Iditarod sled dog race.
Well, the window is closing today for registering to vote for the midterm elections in some
states and Pierre Hansi Lo Wang has that story.
There are only hours left for eligible voters to register or update their registration in
time for the midterms in Kansas, Louisiana, New Jersey, Oregon, and West Virginia.
And there's less than a week left until the next major voter registration deadline on
Monday, October 19th.
That's in three states, Alabama, Pennsylvania, and South Dakota, as well as Guam.
If you're already registered, election officials recommend confirming your status and updating
your contact information before the deadline.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their
name or haven't voted in a while.
You can check your voter registration status by visiting your state or territory's official
election website.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
It is sentencing day for Dwayne Kefi D. Davis, the only person charged with the murder of
the legendary hip hop artist and actor Tupac Shakur more than 30 years ago.
This is NPR News.
New research from the AI company Anthropik suggests some AI might soon be able to replicate
inside smart devices.
Here's NPR's Jeff Brumfield.
Anthropik warned that AI models could soon spread inside networked devices around the
house, including smart refrigerators, televisions, and even robotic vacuum cleaners.
Researchers demonstrated such replication inside some cheap TV boxes and with simulations.
The researchers warned AI worms would be similar to existing computer viruses, but they would
be more adaptable and could be hard to shut down.
The best defense against AI and regular viruses alike?
A strong password for every smart device in your home.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
Formula One has signed a 10-year deal with Rwanda to host Grand Prix races starting in
the early 2030s.
More from NPR's Jewel Wright.
Formula One says the races will be called the African Grand Prix and will be held on the
new Popol's-built circuit in Bugesera, near Rwanda's capital, Kigali.
It will be the first F1 race in Africa since the 1993 South African Grand Prix.
F1 officials say they hope the race will offer an opportunity for the sport to expand its
profile across Africa.
Rwanda's President Paul Kagami has held the deal, saying it will attract skills, tourism,
and investment to Rwanda.
However, the event is likely to face opposition from human rights groups who have accused Rwanda
of using sports to improve its international image amid widespread government crackdowns
on political opposition and press freedom.
Jewel Wright, NPR News, Vegas.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.

topics.text: Zelensky tells NPR the Trump administration warned it could cut Ukraine's intelligence sharing over refinery strikes
Zelensky says lifting Russian diesel sanctions won't lower fuel prices, blames Strait of Hormuz blockage
Trump says US is sharing intelligence with Ukraine and working with Russia to end the war
Trump travels to Alaska to rally for Senator Dan Sullivan in Wasilla ahead of midterms
Voter registration deadlines approach in Kansas, Louisiana, New Jersey, Oregon, West Virginia, and others
Sentencing day for Duane Davis, the only person charged in the murder of Tupac Shakur
Anthropic research suggests AI could soon replicate across networked smart home devices
Formula One signs 10-year deal to host African Grand Prix in Rwanda starting early 2030s
